Technical details:
# TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal trigger route is silent on STM32U5A5JTxQ — DAC sees no triggers despite correct CR config **Repository:** STM32CubeU5 **Versions affected:** - CMSIS device: V1.4.2.0 - HAL: V1.6.x - Affected chip: STM32U5A5JTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q **Related upstream issues (same family):** - [#69](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/issues/69) ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one - [#70](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/issues/70) LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger silent This is a third instance of an internal trigger-routing path that is silently silent on this U5A5 silicon — the source generates the event, the destination is correctly configured to receive it, but no event ever reaches the destination. All three involve the chained on-chip trigger paths the U5A5 advertises. ## Severity The standard "TIM1 paces DAC1 via TRGO" pattern — well-supported across the F4 / H7 / G4 families — fails silently on U5A5: DAC1 stops accepting triggers, DOR1 never advances, and any DMA chain feeding DHR1 stalls because the DAC stops requesting refills. No HAL call returns an error. ## Bench reproduction NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q with a project where: - DAC1 activated, channel 1 on PA4 (DAC_OUT1). - hdac1.Init (per CubeMX): DAC_Trigger = DAC_TRIGGER_T1_TRGO, output buffer enabled, no autonomous mode. - TIM1 configured at 1 kHz (Prescaler = 159, Period = 999) with Init.MasterOutputTrigger = TIM_TRGO_UPDATE (set via HAL_TIMEx_MasterConfigSynchronization). - DMA chain attached via HAL_DAC_Start_DMA(&hdac1, DAC_CHANNEL_1, sine_table, 100, DAC_ALIGN_12B_R). Read at runtime: DAC1->CR = 0x00002007 EN1=1, TEN1=1, TSEL1[0]=1 (TSEL1 = 0001 = TIM1_TRGO per HAL), DMAEN1=1. All correct per the IOC. DAC1->DOR1 = 0 stuck at 0 forever — DAC never transferred DHR1 → DOR1. DAC1->SR = 0x00000800 BWST = 1 (busy-write-status) — DAC waiting for trigger. TIM1->CR1 = 0x00000001 counter enabled, ticking at 1 kHz (CNT advancing). TIM1->CR2 = 0x00000020 MMS = 010 = UPDATE event TRGO source. Verified. GPDMA1_Ch11.CCR = 0x00005f00 channel disabled (EN=0); CSR=IDLE. GPDMA1_Ch11.CBR1 = 0x000000be 190 of 200 bytes remaining — only 5 samples written before the chain stalled because DAC stopped requesting more. ## Isolation evidence The same DAC + DMA + trigger setup with the trigger-source field changed in user code: c DAC1->CR &= ~(0xFUL << 2); /* clear TSEL1 */ DAC1->CR |= (0x8UL << 2) | (1UL << 1); /* TSEL1 = 1000 = TIM15_TRGO, TEN1 = 1 */ — *with TIM15 also at 1 kHz Update Event* — produces the expected behaviour: DOR1 advances on each TIM15 update, the DMA refills DHR1 cleanly, the sine waveform appears on PA4. Switching back to TSEL1 = 0001 (TIM1_TRGO) silences the chain again. Software trigger (TSEL1 = 0000, then pulse DAC1->SWTRIGR = 1) also works: DOR1 follows DHR1 on each pulse. So the DAC's trigger acceptance mechanism is functional — only the specific TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal route is silent. ## Suspected root cause Either: - A device-header off-by-one in the DAC_TRIGGER_T1_TRGO macro encoding (analogous to the ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos issue in #69), where the TSEL1 value 0001 actually maps to a different (silent) trigger source on this silicon than the HAL believes. - Or a silicon-level routing issue between TIM1's TRGO output and the DAC1 trigger input mux, possibly requiring an additional enable bit somewhere outside the DAC's own CR. I haven't been able to discriminate between these without ST's RTL or trigger-mux documentation. The diagnostic steps above are sufficient to reproduce the silent-trigger symptom; the fix requires ST internal information. ## Workaround Substitute a different timer's TRGO (e.g. TIM15_TRGO via TSEL1 = 1000). Verified working at 1 kHz with the rest of the chain unchanged.

Fix: # LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ, HAL, ADC, bug_report, low, bug, lptim, LPTIM1_CH1, ADC4, CFGR1, EXTSEL, TIM2_TRGO

Technical details:
# LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.EXTSEL = 5 correctly set **Related:** depends on the workaround from issue #69 (override CFGR1.EXTSEL in user code) being applied first — without it EXTSEL is 010 (TIM2_TRGO) instead of 101 (LPTIM1_CH1) and this bug is masked by the wrong-trigger symptom. **Repository:** STM32CubeU5 (HAL or device header — exact root cause not isolated) **Versions affected:** - CMSIS device: V1.4.2.0 - HAL: V1.6.x - Affected chip: STM32U5A5JTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q ## Severity ADC4 with LPTIM1_CH1 trigger source never starts converting, even though LPTIM1 internally completes compare-match events. The LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 EXT trigger route is silent. Any low-power "sample-then-sleep" pattern that depends on this combination fails to capture data in Stop modes. ## Bench evidence Project setup: - ADC4 activated, channel 4 (PC3) enabled. - hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConv = ADC4_EXTERNALTRIG_LPTIM1_CH1 - hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConvEdge = ADC_EXTERNALTRIGCONVEDGE_RISING - After HAL_ADC_Init, ADC4->CFGR1 is overridden in user code to write the correct EXTSEL bits at silicon position 5-7 (workaround for the separate ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one filed under issue #N). - LPTIM1: kernel clock = LSE 32.768 kHz (verified — RCC->BDCR=0x883 with LSEON=1, LSERDY=1; CCIPR3 LPTIM1SEL = 0b11 = LSE), Init.Period = 32767, channel-1 PWM via HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel(.Pulse=32700, .OCPolarity=LPTIM_OCPOLARITY_HIGH) + HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start(&hlptim1, LPTIM_CHANNEL_1). - LPDMA1 channel 2 allocated for ADC4, circular DMA, 10-sample buffer. Runtime register dump (CPU active, no Stop entry): ADC4->CFGR1 = 0x002005a3 (EXTSEL bits 5..7 = 0b101 = 5 = LPTIM1_CH1) LPTIM1->CR = 0x1 (ENABLE set, running) LPTIM1->ARR = 32767 (matches Init.Period) LPTIM1->CCR1 = 32700 (matches HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel.Pulse) LPTIM1->CCMR1 = 0x2 (CCE = 1, channel-1 enabled, output-compare mode, polarity active high) LPTIM1->ISR = 0x118 (bits 3=CMPM1, 4=ARROK, 8=UE — compare match HAS fired) (bit 0=CMP1OK = 0 ← never sets) (bit 1=ARRM = 0 ← never sets even after seconds) RCC->BDCR = 0x883 (LSEON, LSERDY) RCC->CCIPR3 = 0x4f83 (LPTIM1SEL bits 10-11 = 0b11 = LSE) LPTIM1 CNT was confirmed to advance at the LSE rate by polling: 0 → 3284 over 100 ms (expected ~3276 at 32.768 kHz, well within crystal tolerance). ### What's puzzling about the ISR state - CMPM1 (bit 3 — compare match flag) **does set**, so the comparator is running and matching CCR1. - CMP1OK (bit 0 — CMP1 register update acknowledged) **never sets**, even after explicitly clearing via ICR and re-writing LPTIM1->CCR1 = 32700 with the timer enabled. - ARRM (bit 1 — autoreload match) **never sets** even though the period (~32768 LSE ticks ≈ 1 s) elapses many times. The combination — internal compare matches happen, but the "register update acknowledged" handshake never completes and the autoreload-match flag never latches — suggests the LPTIM-side register-update / event-output path is in some non-standard state. ### What does work - ADC4 + TIM2_TRGO (the trigger ADC4 *actually* sees when CubeMX/HAL writes the wrong CFGR1 — see the EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one report) does deliver triggers and ADC4 converts. - LPTIM1 ARRM IRQ wakes the CPU correctly when used the conventional way (HAL_LPTIM_Counter_Start_IT) — independently verified. So both endpoints work in isolation. Only the chained LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 EXT path fails to deliver. ## What I have not isolated I haven't been able to pin down whether the bug is: 1. A LPTIM HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel / HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start ordering bug that leaves CMP1 in a half-initialized state. 2. An internal silicon route between LPTIM1's compare-match output and the ADC4 trigger input that needs a separate enable bit not exposed via the HAL. 3. A second device-header off-by-one that affects either the LPTIM CCMR1 or the ADC4 trigger-mux register. The minimal repro outlined above is sufficient to reproduce the symptom; isolating between (1)/(2)/(3) would require either ST's RTL/silicon documentation or scope traces of the LPTIM1_CH1 internal trigger line (not externally observable). ## Workaround currently in use CPU-mediated 1 Hz sampling: LPTIM1's ARRM IRQ wakes the CPU each second, the CPU triggers a single ADC4 conversion via HAL_ADC_Start(&hadc4), reads the value, stores it, and re-enters Stop 2. Power consumption is slightly higher than a true autonomous chain (CPU briefly active each cycle) but the sample-then-sleep pattern still demonstrates µA-class operation.

Key comments:
Hello @pbwarmu017, Thank you for this report, since https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/issues/69 analyzed and there is no incorrect definition of macros bits. I guess so there is other restriction and I would like to draw your attention to **the note in EXTSEL bits description** shown below: > Bits 8:6 EXTSEL[2:0]: External trigger selection > These bits select the external event used to trigger the start of conversion (refer to table ADC > interconnection in Section 34.4.2: ADC pins and internal signals for details): > 000: adc_trg0 > 001: adc_trg1 > 010: adc_trg2 > 011: adc_trg3 > 100: adc_trg4 > 101: adc_trg5 > 110: adc_trg6 > 111: adc_trg7 > **Note: The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART bit is cleared to 0 by writing > ADSTP to 1 (this ensures that no conversion is ongoing).** Therefore, I advise you to use the correct ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos = 6U and set **ADSTP** in the **CR** register to **1** before **EXTSEL** setting. Please, do not hesitate to ask if there is anything unclear. KIWA Mohamed Chaker. Thanks for the cross-reference to the analysis on #69. Acknowledging that ADC4 EXTSEL is a 3-bit field at bits 8:6 per RM0456 §34.7.4

Technical details:
# stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits **Repository:** STM32CubeU5 (the device header is bundled here; root cause may be in cmsis_device_u5) **Versions affected:** - CMSIS device: __STM32U5_CMSIS_VERSION = V1.4.2.0 (per stm32u5xx.h lines 94-101) - HAL: __STM32U5xx_HAL_VERSION_MAIN = 0x01, _SUB1 = 0x06 → V1.6.x (per stm32u5xx_hal.c lines 57-58) - Affected chip: STM32U5A5JTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q (stm32u5a5xx.h) ## Severity **Silent miscompile of every ADC4 trigger-source selection.** The HAL writes the trigger-source bits into the wrong positions of ADC4->CFGR1. Code that asks for ADC4_EXTERNALTRIG_LPTIM1_CH1 ends up with EXTSEL field set to 0b010 = TIM2_TRGO. If TIM2 happens to be active in the project, ADC4 fires on its events at high rate; if not, ADC4 silently sees no triggers. Both failure modes are hard to diagnose because nothing returns HAL_ERROR. ## Root cause — single off-by-one in the device header Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32U5xx/Include/stm32u5a5xx.h, lines 3852-3857: c #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos (6UL) #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk (0x7UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) /*!< 0x000003E0 */ #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_0 (0x01UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) /*!< 0x00000020 */ #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_1 (0x02UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) /*!< 0x00000040 */ #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_2 (0x04UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) /*!< 0x00000080 */ The comments next to the constants — 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0x3E0 — are correct values for Pos = 5. The actual preprocessor expansion uses Pos = 6, producing **0x40, 0x80, 0x100** (one bit too far left) and a mask of **0x1C0** (not 0x3E0). The _Msk comment compounds the contradiction by claiming 0x000003E0 while the macro evaluates to 0x000001C0. For comparison, the equivalent ADC1 group at lines 3793-3800 uses ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos = 5UL and the comments match the macro values: c #define ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos (5UL) #define ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk (0x1FUL << ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) /*!< 0x000003E0 */ ... ADC1 is correct; ADC4 has the typo. ## What goes wrong downstream Drivers/STM32U5xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32u5xx_ll_adc.h builds ADC4 trigger-source values from these constants. For example: c #define LL_ADC_REG_TRIG_EXT_LPTIM1_CH1_ADC4 \ (ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_2 | ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_0 | ADC_REG_TRIG_EXT_EDGE_DEFAULT) - **Comment-implied value** (Pos=5): 0x80 | 0x20 | 0x400 = 0x4A0 → EXTSEL=5 (LPTIM1_CH1) + EXTEN rising - **Actual macro value** (Pos=6): 0x100 | 0x40 | 0x400 = 0x540 → bit 8 (Reserved) + bit 6 (EXTSEL[1]) + bit 10 (EXTEN rising) HAL_ADC_Init ORs the (wrong) value into CFGR1 directly. The silicon reads the EXTSEL field from bits 5-7, sees 0b010 = 2, and routes the trigger from TIM2_TRGO instead of LPTIM1_CH1. Same arithmetic shift applies to every other LL trigger-source macro in the ADC4 group (TIM1_TRGO2, TIM1_CH4, TIM2_TRGO, TIM15_TRGO, TIM6_TRGO, LPTIM1_CH1, LPTIM3_CH2, EXTI_LINE15). Every one of them lands in the wrong CFGR1 bits. ## Bench reproduction NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q with a project where: - ADC4 is activated, channel 4 (PC3) enabled - hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConv = ADC4_EXTERNALTRIG_LPTIM1_CH1 - hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConvEdge = ADC_EXTERNALTRIGCONVEDGE_RISING - LPTIM1 configured: kernel clock = LSE 32.768 kHz, ARR = 32767, CCR1 = 32700, channel-1 PWM started via HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel + HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start - LPDMA1 channel allocated for ADC4, circular DMA, S = 10 samples Read at runtime *after* HAL_ADC_Init: hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConv = 0x00000540 ← should be 0x000004A0 ADC4->CFGR1 = 0x00200543 ← EXTSEL bits 5..7 = 0b010 = TIM2_TRGO If TIM2 is also active in the project (it commonly is — TIM2 is the standard input-capture timer in early labs), the ADC4 chain captures all 10 samples in well under one second instead of the expected ten seconds. Disabling the user-code call to HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start does **not** stop the conversions — proof that the trigger source is something other than LPTIM1. Forcing EXTSEL = 5 directly: c ADC4->CFGR1 = (ADC4->CFGR1 & ~(0x7UL << 5)) | (0x5UL << 5); restores the correct trigger-source field, but no triggers reach ADC4 in this configuration — there is a separate issue with the LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path that this report does not cover (LPTIM1's CMP1OK flag never sets even though CMPM1 does fire internally). ## Suggested fix diff -#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos (6UL) -#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk (0x7UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) +#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos (5UL) +#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk (0x7UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) After the fix, ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk evaluates to 0xE0 (matching the actual silicon field at bits 5-7 — note the existing /*!< 0x000003E0 */ comment overstates the field width and should also be updated to 0x000000E0). Verified: writing the corrected EXTSEL=5 value (0xA0) into the EXTSEL field of CFGR1 directly is what the LL macros need to produce. ## Workaround for downstream code Until the header is fixed, projects that select an ADC4 trigger source must override CFGR1.EXTSEL after HAL_ADC_Init: c HAL_ADC_Init(&hadc4); /* Workaround for ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one in stm32u5a5xx.h: write * the EXTSEL field at its correct silicon position (bits 5..7). Replace * the literal 0x5 with 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 per the trigger source you want. */ ADC4->CFGR1 = (ADC4->CFGR1 & ~(0x7UL << 5)) | (0x5UL << 5);

Hello @pbwarmu017, Thank you for your report, it seems that point don't makes sense. According to the [Reference Manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) of U5 and 34.7.4 ADC configuration register 1 (ADC_CFGR1) section which describe clearly EXTSEL bits this definition of macros bits is correct. [IMAGE ATTACHED] Therefore, please allow to close this issue, thank you for your understanding. Mohamed Chaker KIWA. Acknowledging that the macro itself is correct per RM0456 §34.7.4 — ADC4's EXTSEL is a 3-bit field at bits 8:6 (_Pos = 6, _Msk = 0x7UL << 6 = 0x1C0), and my earlier framing of the macro position as the bug was wrong. What remains is a smaller documentation inconsistency in the same header section. The inline comments next to the four EXTSEL lines in Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32U5xx/Include/stm32u5a5xx.h show values that correspond to _Pos = 5 (the ADC1-style 5-bit layout), not the actual _Pos = 6 3-bit layout: c #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos (6UL) #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk (0x7UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos) /*!< 0x000003E0 */ #define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL

Technical details:
# LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5) ## Summary When an LPBAM scenario contains an **I2C Master_Transmit node** with the DevAddress field set to a 7-bit slave address (the value the CubeMX scenario designer accepts), the actual address byte transmitted on the I2C bus is **not** the expected value. The I2C peripheral sends an address byte that the slave does not recognise, so the slave does not ACK, no data is exchanged, and the response buffer stays at its uninitialised value forever. This appears to be an interaction between (a) the CubeMX scenario designer's input validation (which accepts only 7-bit values, max 127) and (b) the LPBAM library's CR2.SADD encoding in STM32CubeU5/Utilities/lpbam/STM32U5/stm32_ll_lpbam.c (which OR's the raw DevAddress value into CR2 without shifting). ## Affected versions - STM32CubeU5 firmware: as included in STM32CubeMX 6.17 (verified locally May 2026) - Target: STM32U5A5ZJTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q - TrustZone: disabled (the bug is independent of TZ) ## Reproduction project Minimal CubeMX project, ~200 lines of user code, single I2C3 peripheral. ### CubeMX setup - Board Selector: NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q - TrustZone: **Disabled** - HSE: Crystal/Resonator (16 MHz, X3 on-board crystal) - PLL → SYSCLK 160 MHz, Range 1, EPOD on - Peripherals enabled: - **USART1** (Async, 115200 8N1, PA9/PA10 for VCP) - **I2C3** (Standard mode 100 kHz, PC0/PC1, **autonomous mode disabled**) - **LPTIM1** (Counter mode, ARR=32767) - **LPDMA1** Channel 1 - LPBAM Application "LpbamAp1" with one queue containing 3 nodes: 1. LPTIM1.Start (continuous mode) 2. I2C3.MasterTx — 1 byte, **DevAddress = 80 (0x50)**, no LPDMA trigger, AUTOEND, 7-bit 3. I2C3.MasterRx — 8 bytes, **DevAddress = 80 (0x50)**, LPDMA trigger = LPTIM1 CH1 rising, AUTOEND, 7-bit ### Hardware - AT24C02 EEPROM (DIP-8) on I2C3: - Pin 1-3 (A0/A1/A2): GND → slave address 0x50 - Pin 4: GND - Pin 5 (SDA): PC1 (CN9-9) - Pin 6 (SCL): PC0 (CN9-11) - Pin 7 (WP): GND - Pin 8 (VCC): 3V3 Internal pull-ups enabled in user code on PC0/PC1 (~40 kΩ — adequate for 100 kHz). ### Linker script + manual edits required to make the project build CubeMX 6.17 generates an incomplete LPBAM scenario for this configuration: 1. **lpbam_lpbamap1_scenario_config.c is not generated** — the header declares MX_LpbamAp1_Scenario_Init/Link/Start but no implementation exists. We hand-wrote stub implementations. 2. **__attribute__((section(".lpbam_section"))) is not applied** to the LPBAM node descriptors — they land in main SRAM (0x20...) instead of SRAM4 (0x28...). Added manually inside the USER CODE BEGIN Queue*_Desc blocks (regen-survivable). 3. **extern declarations** for the user data buffers (lpbam_cmd, lpbam_resp defined in main.c) had to be added in scenario_build.c USER CODE EV block. 4. **Linker script SRAM4 section** (.lpbam_section (NOLOAD) >SRAM4) added manually. Each of those four items is arguably a separate CubeMX shortcoming. The bug below is independent of all of them — once the buffers and descriptors are confirmed in SRAM4, the address-encoding bug still occurs. ## Expected vs Actual ### Expected (based on standard CubeMX I2C semantics) Setting DevAddress = 80 (= 0x50, the 7-bit AT24C02 address — the value the GUI accepts as a valid 7-bit address) should result in the I2C peripheral transmitting the address byte 0xA0 (= 0x50 << 1 with R/W=0) on the bus. The AT24C02 ACKs, and the chain proceeds. ### Actual A logic-analyzer capture of the bus shows the address byte decoded as 0x00 (general-call address). The AT24C02 does not ACK its own address (which is 0x50, not 0x00). The data byte the master attempts to send (the EEPROM memory pointer 0x00) is NACK'd along with the address. The response buffer lpbam_resp is never updated. ### VCP output (after power-cycle to clear SRAM) === LPBAM single-byte MasterTx repro === I2C3 scan: 0x50 EEPROM page-write [C0..C7] @ 0x00: HAL=0 EEPROM verify-read: HAL=0, bytes = C0 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 LPBAM scenario built: 15 nodes starting at 0x2800000C Buffer addrs: lpbam_cmd=0x28000000 lpbam_resp=0x28000004 (SRAM4 = 0x28xxxxxx) LPBAM started — observing chain output: cycle 1: B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F cycle 2: B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F cycle 3: B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F The B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F is uninitialised SRAM4 garbage that never gets overwritten by the LPBAM chain. The pre-pop verify confirms the EEPROM is wired correctly and contains C0..C7 at addresses 0..7 — the LPBAM read just isn't reaching it. ### Bus decode write to 0x00 ack data: 0x00 Each LPTIM1 cycle the bus shows two transactions: a 2-byte write to address 0x00 followed by an 8-byte read attempt that returns no ACKs. ## Root-cause analysis (preliminary) Looking at Utilities/lpbam/STM32U5/stm32_ll_lpbam.c line 1131: c case LPBAM_I2C_CONFIG_TRANSACTION_ID: { ... dummy = pConfNode->pInstance->CR2; // line 1122 *pConfNode->NodeDesc.pSrcVarReg = dummy | I2C_CR2_STOP; // line 1125 if ((mode is master)) { dummy |= I2C_CR2_START | I2C_CR2_RELOAD | I2C_CR2_AUTOEND | I2C_CR2_RD_WRN | pConfNode->Config.DevAddress // line 1131 | ((uint32_t)pConfNode->Config.Size << I2C_CR2_NBYTES_Pos); ... if (master TX) dummy &= ~I2C_CR2_RD_WRN; // line 1265 dummy |= AddressingMode << I2C_CR2_ADD10_Pos; // line 1269 *pConfNode->NodeDesc.pSrcVarReg = dummy | DevAddress; // line 1272 } } The library OR's DevAddress directly into CR2's lower bits (SADD[9:0]). For 7-bit addressing, the I2C peripheral expects the actual 7-bit address in SADD[7:1] (i.e. shifted left by 1). With DevAddress=80 the SADD field ends up = 0x50, which the peripheral interprets as SADD[7:1] = 0x28 → bus byte = 0x50/0x51 → an analyzer would decode this as 7-bit address 0x28, not the intended 0x50. But the bus trace decodes as 0x00, not 0x28 — so there is *additional* corruption beyond just the missing left-shift. Possibilities: the write at line 1125 (dummy | I2C_CR2_STOP, which has SADD bits zero) is going to the same descriptor and clobbering the SADD bits set at line 1272; or a separate later descriptor re-writes CR2 with stale STOP bits; or the I2C peripheral responds to the multi-step LPDMA write sequence in a way that ends with SADD cleared. We did **not** fully isolate which of these is at fault. Manually patching DevAddress to a pre-shifted value (e.g. 0xA0 for slave 0x50) bakes the descriptor's CR2 source value correctly in SRAM (verified by reading the LPBAM source words after MX_*_Scenario_Build) — yet the bus still shows an incorrect address. Something at runtime, after LPDMA writes the descriptor's source value to CR2, is corrupting the SADD field. ## Workaround Restrict LPBAM I2C scenarios to **MasterRx-only** chains (single-node, hardware-triggered). Reading from a peripheral that doesn't require an address-pointer write avoids the MasterTx node entirely. The bug above prevents any single-byte MasterTx from completing successfully on the bus. ## Asks of ST 1. Document the DevAddress encoding convention expected by the LPBAM I2C node — is it raw (already shifted) or 7-bit (lib should shift)? 2. Fix the CubeMX scenario designer to (a) accept the matching encoding and (b) reject invalid values upfront. 3. Fix the runtime address corruption that causes bus to show 0x00 even when the descriptor's SADD bits are correct in SRAM. 4. Make the manual fixes listed above (scenario_config.c generation, NODE_SECTION attribute, extern decls, linker section) part of CubeMX's standard LPBAM output. ## Files - Reproduction project (zip attached) - VCP capture (inline above) [main_user_code_scaffold.c](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27558288/main_user_code_scaffold.c) [LPBAM-scenario.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27558387/LPBAM-scenario.zip)

Technical details:
**Setup Description**: We used a circular LPBAM setup involving LPDMA, LPADC, LPTIM, and LPGPIO peripherals. **Bug Description**: As stated in the title, the LPBAM application scenario fails to be successfully created after updating the STM32U5 HAL from v1.5.0 to v1.7.0 (STM32CubeU5). **Steps to Reproduce**: Initializing the LPBAM circular application. **Expected Behavior**: The LPBAM circular application should be successfully created. **Observed Behavior**: The LPBAM application fails to be created successfully, showing an error indicating that the node cannot be found when setting LPBAM circular mode to a linked-list queue based on the selected descriptor and node level. Call hierarchy to error: - LPBAM_Status_t ADV_LPBAM_Q_SetCircularMode(...) - HAL_DMAEx_List_SetCircularModeConfig(...) - DMA_List_FindNode(...) - if (currentnode_address != ((uint32_t)pNode & DMA_CLLR_LA)) Additionally, an interesting observation is that when compiler optimizations are enabled (tested with size optimization and debug optimization), the function ADV_LPBAM_Q_SetCircularMode(...) returns an error. However, when optimizations are disabled, the function does not return an error, but the result remains the same—the LPBAM peripherals mentioned above do not function as expected. **Additional Explanation**: If we move ADV_LPBAM_Q_SetCircularMode immediately after setting the node as the start of the circular linked list, the function successfully finds the node and sets it as the start of the list. However, we still encounter issues with other LPBAM peripherals used in this application. During debugging, we identified a few lines of code that were modified between HAL versions and appear to introduce this issue. When these lines are commented out, everything functions as expected. We would like to clarify their exact purpose. Problematic Lines: - File: stm32u5xx_hal_dma_ex.c - Function: DMA_List_BuildNode(...) - Lines:** 3902-3912 - Specific case affecting us: [3911: pNode->LinkRegisters[NODE_CLLR_LINEAR_DEFAULT_OFFSET] = 0U;] While it's clear that these lines were added to reset the node during initialization, could it be possible that the previous node in the linked list is being overwritten during the creation of the circular LPBAM application?

Method description reads: _modify bash /batch variable value with layout file content_ Essentially, this method allows to update shell script variable values based on macro-preprocessed C file like [image_macros_to_preprocess_bl2.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Projects/B-U585I-IOT02A/Applications/SBSFU/SBSFU_Boot/Src/image_macros_to_preprocess_bl2.c) or this test example: C enum image_attributes { RE_IMAGE_FLASH_NON_SECURE_IMAGE_SIZE = (0x20000 - (0x10000 + 0x8000)) // yields 0x18000 instead of 0x8000 }; After running this command: ./Middlewares/mcuboot/scripts/dist/imgtool/imgtool.exe flash --layout ./<my_path>/test.c -b image_ns_size -m RE_IMAGE_FLASH_NON_SECURE_IMAGE_SIZE -s 0 ./test.sh **image_ns_size** variable value in **test.sh** script should get updated to **0x8000** value but it does not. Instead, **0x18000** value gets written. Test files attached. [test.zip](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/files/14999760/test.zip) The current implementation does not always correctly subtract values. The culprit is [macro_parser.py](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Middlewares/Third_Party/mcuboot/scripts/imgtool/macro_parser.py) where this problem is even mentioned but it is not a solution, it is a particularly nasty trap. I lost many hours before I found out what I described here. I am not a Python expert but probably there are at least several way better approaches that could be used like [py-expression](https://github.com/data7expressions/py-expression), [pyparsing](https://github.com/pyparsing/pyparsing/) or [lark parser](https://github.com/lark-parser/lark) ([sample code](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67491514/9972769)) - see how easy it is to use. There are also other problems with this tool. 1) In case file path does not exist, misleading _"local variable 'value' referenced before assignment"_ error message is displayed. 2) Unlike the output file path, input file path must be absolute. Why command modifying scripts is named flash? Perhaps more adequate name could be used. Why is this function part of the imgtool at all? It has very little to do with image creation. A separate tool would be much better, especially if one wants/needs to use the latest original imgtool version.

Problem: CRYP Key & IV configuration does not respect configured DataType
Context: repo=STM32CubeU5, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=42
Root cause: Hello @fermentedfly, Thank you for reporting.
Fix: stm32u5xx_hal_cryp We use AES in byte mode (CRYP_DATATYPE_8B).
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, bug, AES, CRYP_DATATYPE_8B, CRYP_ConfigTypeDef, KEY, CRYP_DATATYPE_32B, CRYP_SetIV, CRYP_HandleTypeDef, CRYP_SetKey

Technical details:
stm32u5xx_hal_cryp We use AES in byte mode (CRYP_DATATYPE_8B). CRYP_ConfigTypeDef provides the option to set the DataType. This works fine for the data fed into AES but KEY & IV are passed in in mode CRYP_DATATYPE_32B regardless of the setup of DataType. see static void CRYP_SetIV(CRYP_HandleTypeDef *hcryp) & static void CRYP_SetKey(CRYP_HandleTypeDef *hcryp, uint32_t KeySize). This is especially problematic since key & iv are not passed to the hardware registers during HAL_CRYP_Init or HAL_CRYP_SetConfig but when calling HAL_CRYP_Encrypt which means we can't use local (stack) variables to correct the data alignment ourselves. Please update CRYP_SetIV & CRYP_SetKey so they can deal with all modes of DataType. Thanks, Manuel

Key comments:
Hello @fermentedfly, Thank you for reporting. Would you please clarify your problem do you want to have the ability to changes DataType into the Key and initialization vector. Otherwise, you should first call HAL_CRYP_SetConfig then HAL_CRYP_Init and then HAL_CRYP_Encrypt I've attached a demo. testCBCNoSwap() passes key, IV, and data in big-endian, with DataType set to CRYP_NO_SWAP. This is similar to some examples in STM32Cube and works. testCBCByteSwap() passes key, IV, and data in little-endian, with DataType set to CRYP_BYTE_SWAP. This **fails**. I've had a look into stm32u5xx_hal_cryp.c, the cause for the failure is that key and IV are always interpreted as being in big-endian, regardless of DataType. testCBCByteSwapKeyIVBigEndian() passes key and IV in big-endian and data in little-endian, with DataType set to CRYP_BYTE_SWAP. This works. Herein lies the problem: There is no way to pass key and IV in little-endian, which is an issue for my application. void testCBCNoSwap() { __HAL_RCC_AES_CLK_ENABLE(); // https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/Cryptographic-Algorithm-Validation-Program/documents/aes/aesmmt.zip // CBCMMT128.rsp Encrypt Count 0 //

Root cause: Hi @wooyay, The HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback() is supposed to be **customized by users** depending on the needs of their applications.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** - STM32U575I-EV evaluation board - STM32CubeU5 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, USB, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, projects, STM32U575I-EV, USBX, STM32, Ux_Host_HID, NAK

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** - STM32U575I-EV evaluation board - STM32CubeU5 1.4.0 - STM32CubeIDE 1.14.1 **Describe the bug (skip if none)** USB endpoints that declare a 1 ms polling interval are not correctly handled by the USBX STM32 host controller driver. **How to reproduce the bug (skip if none)** 1. Program the Ux_Host_HID example to the board and configure the board jumpers. 2. Attach a Low Speed mouse to the host port and observe expected behaviour - interrupt endpoint is polled every 8 ms with data being returned when available. 3. Attach a Full Speed mouse with an endpoint that has a 1 ms pollinig interval to the host port. The interrupt endpoint stops being polled after the first NAK. Note that this is not limited to Ux_Host_HID or HID devices. It affects any USB endpoint that sets a 1 ms periodic interval. **Additional context** Investigation shows that when the endpoint is created the interval mask is set as 0 as expected to force the scheduler to queue the host channel every frame. In _ux_hcd_stm32_perioidic_schedule() the scheduler mode is set: c /* If it's scheduled each SOF/uSOF, the request should be submitted * immediately after packet is done. This is performed in callback. */ if (ed -> ux_stm32_ed_interval_mask == 0) ed -> ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode = 0; However, HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback() does not appear to handle the case where urb_state == URB_NOTREADY and ed -> ux_stm32_ed_type == EP_TYPE_INTR (and possibly EP_TYPE_ISOC) so the transmit request is never resubmitted.

Key comments:
Hi @wooyay, The HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback() is supposed to be **customized by users** depending on the needs of their applications. In your case, are you referring to the __weak callback at the [driver level](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/f1946d68701260860cdb5eae9f7bc5c3ff7f1cd1/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_hcd.c#L733-L743) or to a redefined one in one of the of the [USBx applications](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/tree/main/Projects/STM32U575I-EV/Applications/USBX) provided within this firmware? Regarding the handling of the case urb_state == URB_NOTREADY, it seems handled at the middleware library level, as shown below: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/c8fcb26ff629cf7c2a3b2c60e6121625eaa5ca2d/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_callback.c#L421-L435 Regarding endpoint types EP_TYPE_INTR and EP_TYPE_ISOC handling in case urb_state == URB_NOTREADY, they are handled at driver level in function HAL_HCD_HC_SubmitRequest() as you can see from [this](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/f1946d68701260860cdb5eae9f7bc5c3ff7f1cd1/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_hcd.c#L

To avoid this I modified the example code as follow. void fx_app_thread_entry(ULONG thread_input) { UINT nor_ospi_status = FX_SUCCESS; /* USER CODE BEGIN fx_app_thread_entry 0*/ ULONG bytes_read; ULONG available_space_pre; // Sectors per track if (nor_ospi_status != FX_SUCCESS) { while(1); } nor_ospi_status = fx_media_open(&nor_ospi_flash_disk, FX_NOR_OSPI_VOLUME_NAME, fx_stm32_levelx_nor_driver, (VOID *)LX_NOR_OSPI_DRIVER_ID, (VOID *) fx_nor_ospi_media_memory, sizeof(fx_nor_ospi_media_memory)); Technical details:
1. File [stm32u5a9xx.h](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32U5xx/Include/stm32u5a9xx.h), line 27339: #define USB_OTG_GCCFG_FSVMINUS_Msk 0x1U << USB_OTG_GCCFG_FSVMINUS_Pos) /*!< 0x00000004 */ has missing opening parenthesis! 2. GINTSTS.RSTDET register field definition (USB_OTG_GINTSTS_RSTDET) is missing. See: [RM0456](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf), 73.14.6 OTG core interrupt register [alternate] (OTG_GINTSTS) 3. Many USB_OTG register field names differ from those described in [RM0456](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf). Some of them are completely different. Examples: GINTSTS.WKUPINT -> USB_OTG_GINTSTS_WKUINT GINTSTS.IPXFR -> USB_OTG_GINTSTS_PXFR_INCOMPISOOUT GINTSTS.GONAKEFF -> USB_OTG_GINTSTS_BOUTNAKEFF GCCFG.FORCEHOSTPD -> USB_OTG_GCCFG_PULLDOWNEN GCCFG.VBVALOVEN -> USB_OTG_GCCFG_VBVALEXTOEN GCCFG.HVDMSRCEN -> USB_OTG_GCCFG_H_VDMSRCEN GCCFG.HCDPDETEN -> USB_OTG_GCCFG_H_CDPDETEN GCCFG.HCDPEN -> USB_OTG_GCCFG_H_CDPEN 4. It is difficult to understand why only one particular register - OTG_HPRT ([RM0456](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf), 73.14.30) is defined as USBx_HPRT0 in [stm32u5xx_ll_usb.h](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/7942fc4ea05026e4e9ce72d680f704e9433bce42/Drivers/STM32U5xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32u5xx_ll_usb.h#L517C89-L517C89) header, rather than in [stm32u5a9xx.h](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32U5xx/Include/stm32u5a9xx.h) where it belongs to. USB_OTG_HostTypeDef might be a better place to define it. The same time, this register's fields are defined in [stm32u5a9xx.h](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32U5xx/Include/stm32u5a9xx.h) and correctly named USB_OTG_HPRT_PSPD etc. Not to mention that USBx_HPRT0 definition depends on USBx_BASE defined later like [this](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/7942fc4ea05026e4e9ce72d680f704e9433bce42/Drivers/STM32U5xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32u5xx_ll_usb.c#L1253). I think it is overengineered and overcomplicated. **OTG host supports only one port.** If one really feels like more then one USB port needs to be handled in the future, why not to simply define USB1_HPRT0? - just like e.g. UCPD1 is defined. This is just inconsistent with how other IPs' registers are defined. It is difficult to avoid impression that this STM32U5 HAL release was prepared in rush and never updated after the first [RM0456](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) release version had been finalized.

## Describe the set-up - This bug can be reproduced in 535xx and 545xx based systems - Compiler: Arm GNU Toolchain 12.2.MPACBTI-Bet1 ## Describe the bug When performing the calibration procedure for the ADC1 peripheral through the _HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start_ function, with mode=ADC_CALIB_OFFSET and for single ended channels, the system will either hang/crash or the ADC peripheral won't work correctly, though the configuration is correct. I pinned the problem to the following part of the RM: **Reading calibration factor procedure** (under section 33.4.8) > Once the calibration is complete (ADCAL bit cleared by hardware), the calibration factor can be read using the ADC_CALFACT2 register. > **Nine read accesses** are required to perform this operation[...] These nine access are effectively not performed in the aforementioned function, as interacting with CALFACT2 takes place in the following part of code (**stm32u5xx_hal_adc_ex**:203): c /* Assess whether extended calibration is available on the selected device */ if ((dev_id == 0x455UL) || (dev_id == 0x476UL) || (((dev_id == 0x481UL) || (dev_id == 0x482UL)) && (rev_id >= 0x3000UL))) { /* Perform extended calibration */ /* Refer to ref manual for extended calibration procedure details */ tmp_hal_status = ADC_Enable(hadc); if (tmp_hal_status == HAL_OK) { MODIFY_REG(hadc->Instance->CR, ADC_CR_CALINDEX, 0x9UL << ADC_CR_CALINDEX_Pos); MODIFY_REG(hadc->Instance->CALFACT2, 0x00FF0000UL, 0x00020000UL); SET_BIT(hadc->Instance->CALFACT, ADC_CALFACT_LATCH_COEF); ## How to reproduce the bug 1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project - This particular part of the code is responsible for acquiring a single ended signal at a frequency of 5Khz 2. List the modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem - the responsible driver is implemented in stm32u5xx_hal_adc_ex.c::HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start 3. Describe the use case that generates the problem - See 1. 4. How we can reproduce the problem - Setup the ADC and all related clock settings for acquiring a single ended channel - (optional) Setup the ADC trigger source as a timer - Start calibration procedure via HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start - The system either hangs, crashes, or if not, the ADC will always result in a wrong DR value (0 in my case) after starting the acquisition process (or the timer as in this case) **Additional context** Following the advice contained in the RM (i.e. performing 9 read accesses to CALFACT2), I managed to solve the issue by adding the following lines in _HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start_ (from line 213 onwards): c MODIFY_REG(hadc->Instance->CR, ADC_CR_CALINDEX, 0x9UL << ADC_CR_CALINDEX_Pos); for(uint8_t idx = 0; idx <9; idx ++) { volatile __unused uint32_t foobar= READ_REG(hadc->Instance->CALFACT2); } MODIFY_REG(hadc->Instance->CALFACT2, 0x00FF0000UL, 0x00020000UL); for(uint8_t idx = 0; idx <9; idx ++) { volatile __unused uint32_t foobar= READ_REG(hadc->Instance->CALFACT2); } SET_BIT(hadc->Instance->CALFACT, ADC_CALFACT_LATCH_COEF); I tried removing one of the loops as just a single one should suffice but that didn't solve the problem. ### Notes: - This problem does not appear in 575xx/585xx devices - Optimization can affect patches: the above loops solve the issue even when compiling in Os, a single NOP operation suffices in Og

Problem: DMA_SetConfig() function call not backward compatible with STM32L4 HAL
Context: repo=STM32CubeU5, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=configuration_help, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=22
Root cause: Hello @sdt99 The length of the data to be transferred is mentioned as being in bytes in the HAL U5 directive.
Fix: This isn't a bug as such, but it is a trap for anyone porting from STM32L4 (and maybe other older STM32s) to the U5 HAL.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, DMA, configuration_help, high, invalid, STM32L4, DMA_SetConfig, GPDMA, GPDMA_CxBR1, BNDT, RM0456, DMA_CNDTRx

Technical details:
This isn't a bug as such, but it is a trap for anyone porting from STM32L4 (and maybe other older STM32s) to the U5 HAL. The parameter SrcDataSize in the function DMA_SetConfig() has a different meaning from STM32L4 - this is due to the difference between the U5 GPDMA GPDMA_CxBR1 register BNDT field - which is the number of _bytes_ to transfer (RM0456 17.8.12) and the L4 DMA DMA_CNDTRx register NDT field which is the number of _DMA transfers_ (RM0432, 11.6.4). If the source and destination datawidths are both bytes then DMA_SetConfig() functions identically on the U5 and L4, but if the datawidth is half-word or word then on the U5 the DMA transfer ends after either 1/2 or 1/4 of the DMA is complete since each transfer counts for 2 or 4 bytes, static void DMA_SetConfig(DMA_HandleTypeDef const *const hdma, uint32_t SrcAddress, uint32_t DstAddress, uint32_t SrcDataSize) <<< this parameter is a byte count on the U5 and a transfer count on L4 https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/2e2b3e4733ddcde7af1e91f1c27ef7bea84389ce/Drivers/STM32U5xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_dma.c#L1588 This difference in functionality affects any callers of either HAL_DMA_Start() or HAL_DMA_Start_IT(). It's possible to fix this with conditional compilation in the application code, but it's not ideal to have a near identical HAL API with different functionality. In theory DMA_SetConfig() could read the burst length configured in the hdma struct and multiply the SrcDataSize accordingly and I think that this would lead to a consistent API behavior on the U5 to the L4 - but perhaps it's too late to make this change since it would likely break existing applications. Perhaps a comment above the function prototypes to draw attention to the difference ?

**Describe the set-up** * This behavior is platform independent * Arm GNU Toolchain 12.2.MPACBTI-Bet1 **Describe the bug** Additional delays are inserted in some of the DAC HAL functions, which make use of HAL_Delay timebase function, whose purpose is supposedly avoiding fast switching of the DAC peripheral state, thus enforcing a minimum delay between various operations. Not only can this become cumbersome by itself, as the delay (**1ms**) can be considered quite large in some applications, but the biggest issue at hand is that, should the HAL timebase be temporarily suspended, i.e. because the corresponding timer is paused or the ticker ISR is not called, these functions will completely block the processor in an infinite loop. Affected functions are: HAL_DAC_Start() HAL_DAC_Start_DMA() HAL_DAC_Stop() HAL_DAC_Stop_DMA() HAL_DAC_ConfigChannel() **How to reproduce the bug (skip if none)** 1. How we can reproduce the problem - Recreate context: - Stop the Systick timer, or any timer used for generating the timebase (and thus calling HAL_IncTick on a periodic fashion), or - Enter an ISR with an higher priority than the timebase interrupt, or - Temporarily disable interrupts - Then call one of the aforementioned functions **Additional context** It would be sufficient to remove these HAL_Delay functions inside the DAC HAL. This would also remove the cumbersome 1ms delay which is in most cases unneeded. It should also be noted that this driver is one of the very few introducing these delays, the other being the USB driver and the OPAMP driver. Another possibility would be adding a toggle variable in the DAC HAL that conditionally calls these delays when enabled. At the current state, if maintaining the current HAL version in your own project the solution is simply copy-pasting these functions in equivalent ones without the HAL Delay call, which is **not** an insignificant annoyance

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: ADC oversampling macros incompatible with STM32U575 ADC1 (they are compatible with ADC4)
Context: repo=STM32CubeU5, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-U575ZI, component=ADC, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=18
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 135967
Fix: I discovered this issue while modifying the Nucleo example project: STM32CubeU5\Projects\NUCLEO-U575ZI-Q\Examples\ADC\ADC_DifferentialMode The ADC conversion returns correct 14 bit values when oversampling is disabled: hadc1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-U575ZI, HAL, ADC, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, NUCLEO-U575ZI-Q, ADC_DifferentialMode, DISABLE, ADC_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_64, ADC_RIGHTBITSHIFT_6

Technical details:
I discovered this issue while modifying the Nucleo example project: STM32CubeU5\Projects\NUCLEO-U575ZI-Q\Examples\ADC\ADC_DifferentialMode The ADC conversion returns correct 14 bit values when oversampling is disabled: hadc1.Init.OversamplingMode = DISABLE; When I try to enable oversampling I get incorrect values - to a different extent depending on which oversampling I select. These settings under-read by factor of 3 (0.33) hadc1.Init.Oversampling.Ratio = ADC_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_64; hadc1.Init.Oversampling.RightBitShift = ADC_RIGHTBITSHIFT_6; These settings under-read by factor of 3 (0.83) hadc1.Init.Oversampling.Ratio = ADC_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_16; hadc1.Init.Oversampling.RightBitShift = ADC_RIGHTBITSHIFT_4; I discovered the problem is that the macros ADC_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_16, ADC_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_64, and their corresponding macros LL_ADC_OVS_RATIO_X are copied from earlier HAL, which is compatible with the STM32L4+, but not compatible with the STM32U575 ADC1. The STM32L4 ADC oversampling ratio can only be set as a power of 2 (which corresponds to LL_ADC_OVS_RATIO_X). From RM0432 section 21.6.5 ADC configuration register 2 (ADC_CFGR2): Bits 4:2 OVSR[2:0]: Oversampling ratio This bitfield is set and cleared by software to define the oversampling ratio. 000: 2x 001: 4x 010: 8x 011: 16x 100: 32x 101: 64x 110: 128x 111: 256x The STM32U5 oversampling ratio is set to any number between 1 and 1024. From RM0456 section 29.6.5 ADC configuration register 2 (ADC_CFGR2): Bits 25:16 OSR[9:0]: Oversampling ratio This bitfield is set and cleared by software to define the oversampling ratio. 0: 1x (no oversampling) 1: 2x 2: 3x ... 1023: 1024x Therefore the macros ADC_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_X defined in stm32u5xx_hal_adc.h and LL_ADC_OVS_RATIO_X defined in stm32u5xx_ll_adc.h are not compatible with the STM32U575 ADC1 ADC_CRGR2 register - which can cause confusion when porting a project from an older STM32. Note that these macros do appear to be compatible with ADC4 on the STM32U575 - (according to RM0456 30.7.5 ADC configuration register 2 (ADC_CFGR2)) - so perhaps simply renaming the macros in stm32u5xx_hal_adc.h to ADC4_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_X would make this clearer.
